title: Page Links QA
eyebrow: QA · pull request #333, which fixes #329: a page link in a reply must open

short.lead: The fix is built and open as pull request #333. A reply now counts as linking a page only when the link opens inside the session's folder, and the page builder warns when it writes a page outside that folder. I ran the real end-of-reply hook and the real page builder on both cases, and each behaved as designed. The test suite has no new failures. Only you can test one thing: a real session working in a separate folder.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was checked and how.
items: The real hook flags an outside link

I gave the fix branch's Stop hook a reply linking ../Other/docs/plans/x.html, and it printed: "../Other/docs/plans/x.html is outside this session's folder ..., so the app cannot open it: copy it into .../docs/plans/ and link the copy". Given a reply linking docs/plans/x.html, it printed no page note.

Running make_page.py build with --out pointing outside this folder printed: "... is outside C:\Users\aj\Desktop\ClaudeDev\AjsClaudeCodeTools; a link to it will not open in the app (#329)." A normal build prints no warning (checked by case 834 in verify.py).
9 new cases pass; no new failures

I ran verify.py twice from the branch's folder, and it printed: "RESULT: FAIL - 4 of 856 checks failed" both times. These 4 failing checks (numbers 95, 97, 751 and 835) already failed on main, run from a separate folder, before the change. tools/verify_tools.py printed: "RESULT: PASS - all 47 checks passed".
A worktree session hands you a page that opens

After merging and updating the plugin, ask a session to work in a sibling git worktree and show you a page. The page should open from its link with its content drawn, or the reply should carry the outside-folder note instead of a dead link.
Run it once and tell me what you saw.

changes: One function decides whether a reply links a page.
Any text containing ".html" counted as a page link, and the QA check matched on the file name alone.

An .html link counts only when it resolves inside the session folder. In [x.html](../elsewhere/x.html), the visible text x.html no longer makes it count; only the target ../elsewhere/x.html is checked.
In hook.py: the functions _reply_links_page, _html_paths and _outside_page_links, which four callers use.
Warns when a page lands outside the folder it runs in.
One printed line naming the page, the folder and where to copy it.
In make_page.py, right after the line that prints "wrote".
The section in the systems doc is now marked built and cites line numbers.
The "A page link must open" section said planned.
It now says the section was built in version 2.68.4, cites each function, and lists the 9 test cases.

unverified: No real session in a sibling worktree has run with the fixed plugin yet; I ran the hook directly with a sample payload.
I did not re-run the 4 checks that fail from a separate working folder in the main folder. The pull request's CI run will show whether they pass there.
A bare path with a space in it is cut at the space, so it may be judged against the wrong folder. Markdown links with %20 and file:/// links are decoded first. No case tests a path with a space.

wrapup.summary: A page link now counts only when it opens, and the builder warns when it writes a page outside the session's folder. Pull request #333 waits for your QA.
wrapup.changing: Files changed: hook.py, make_page.py, verify.py, the handover pages systems doc, the state doc and the plugin version.
wrapup.next: On your go-ahead I merge #333 into main. On a fail I fix it on the same branch.
